Hey! Your PR title `tweak (config): make modalities input/output fields optional so that u can specify one without both being required ` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

Thanks for tracking that down — the reasoning_content stripping on replay makes much more sense as the root cause than what I was seeing. The Goose fix is a clean reference for how to handle it. Appreciate you digging into this and sharing the context.

That error confirms the same root cause — the model is truncating mid-string inside the JSON payload, so the `filePath` value gets cut off and the parser chokes on the unterminated string. The skill lookup failure is a downstream consequence of that bad parse, not a separate bug. It does seem to vary by request rather than being consistent, which still points toward something non-deterministic on Moonshot's routing or sampling side. Worth logging the raw response body before any parsing to confirm exactly where the truncation is happening.

That error looks like the model is including the tool namespace prefix in the call (e.g. `glob:glob` instead of just `glob`), which is a different issue from the malformed `input` field I described above. It might be worth checking whether the system prompt or tool definitions being sent to Gemma 4 26B include any namespace metadata that the model is then echoing back in its tool call. If you can share the raw request/response payload it would help narrow down whether this is a prompt formatting issue or something in how Opencode constructs the tool list for that model.

That's a useful data point — if the same key and provider works in kilo code but not here, the issue is almost certainly in how opencode's provider adapter parses or validates the tool call response rather than anything on Moonshot's side. Worth diffing the two adapters' deserialization logic, specifically around how they handle the `input` field when it arrives as a string versus an object. That would narrow it down quickly.

That's a useful data point — the Chinese vs English split suggests it might be a tokenization or prompt handling difference on Moonshot's side rather than a routing issue. Worth filing a bug directly with Moonshot with a minimal repro showing both a Chinese and English version of the same prompt to make the contrast clear. If the malformed `input` field only appears on Chinese prompts, that's a pretty concrete signal for them to act on.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> 
> * [[FEATURE]:Support for multi-agent orchestration in isolated workspaces #17994](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/17994): Similar request for multi-agent orchestration in isolated workspaces — that issue also requests the ability to spawn subagents operating in specific working directories within a monorepo structure.
> 
> If your proposal is meaningfully different (e.g., specifically targeting the `task` tool's `directory` parameter rather than a broader orchestration system), it may help to add a brief note clarifying the distinction from [#17994](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/17994).

Thanks for pointing this out. I agree this overlaps with #17994 in motivation, but I don't think it is a duplicate.

#17994 is a broader request for native multi-agent orchestration / isolated workspaces / worktree lifecycle management. This issue is intentionally much narrower: expose an optional `directory` argument on the existing `task` tool so a child session can run inside the matching `InstanceContext`.

That means no workspace lifecycle, no worktree creation, no merge strategy, and no new orchestration system. The goal is only to let an existing parent agent dispatch an existing subagent into a specific project directory and have cwd, local `.opencode`, `AGENTS.md` walk-up, agents and skills resolve from that directory.

Related PRs I found:

- #17320 fixes re-entering the correct `InstanceContext` for HTTP session routes once a session already has the right directory. It does not let `task` create a child session in a different directory or resolve the subagent/skills from that target directory.
- #9365 adds per-session working directory support for tools, but `task` still creates/forks under the parent `InstanceContext` and resolves the subagent from the parent project.

So this proposal can be a small standalone addition: `task({ ..., directory })` wraps `agent.get`, `sessions.create`, and `ops.prompt` in `InstanceStore.load/provide({ directory })`. When `directory` is omitted, behavior stays exactly as today.

Happy to open a focused PR for just this if the approach sounds acceptable.

That pattern of getting stuck in a loop with malformed bare tool calls is a useful data point — it suggests the model is failing to recover once it enters a bad state, rather than just producing occasional one-off errors. The fact that it works fine through other compatibility layers points to something in how the request or response is being handled on this side rather than a pure model issue. The historical issues you linked are worth cross-referencing to see if any prior workarounds (like stricter prompt framing around tool call format) helped stabilize behavior. Might be worth logging the raw response payloads when the loop starts to see exactly what the model is returning before the adapter parses it.

The websearch and question tool issues sound like they may be separate from the malformed input deserialization problem I described — those look more like the model is hallucinating tool names not in the schema, or the tool list isn't being passed correctly to the Moonshot endpoint. For the JSON parsing errors on bash, it's worth checking whether the model is double-encoding the input field, since that's the same pattern I saw. A quick workaround is to add a normalization step in the provider adapter that detects when `input` is a string and parses it before passing it downstream. No ETA from my side since I'm not a maintainer here, but hopefully someone with more context on the tool registration flow can weigh in.

Good to know the downgrade resolved it for now. For capturing more detail beyond debug logging, intercepting the raw HTTP responses before any parsing happens is usually the most useful — if you can log the raw response body from the provider at the network layer, you can confirm whether the malformed `input` field is coming in that way from Moonshot or being introduced during deserialization. Happy to take a look at any raw payloads you capture if that would help narrow it down.

That's a good lead — if the regression correlates with 1.3.11 it would point squarely at the system prompt change regardless of their eval results. Would be worth bisecting against 1.3.10 to confirm before going back to Moonshot with a concrete reproduction. Happy to test against both versions on our end if that helps narrow it down.

Good clarification, thanks for pointing that out. So the malformed `input` issue we saw was likely unrelated to websearch and more a raw serialization quirk from the Kimi k2.5 endpoint itself. Has anyone confirmed whether the deserialization failures reproduce consistently regardless of which tools are enabled, or is it still intermittent?
